q.q: Which operation removes and returns the topmost element of a stack?
q.x: Push adds to the top, Pop removes from the top, Peek inspects without removing, and Enqueue adds to a queue.

q.q: A circular queue is primarily used to:
o: Avoid the waste of storage space and unnecessary shifting
Increase the processing speed of the CPU
Sort elements in O(n log n)
q.x: A circular queue reuses the front positions, avoiding the 'queue full but space wasted' problem of a linear array queue.

q.q: A stack follows which access order?
q.x: A stack is Last In First Out (LIFO) — the most recently added element is removed first.

q.q: A queue follows which access order?
q.x: A queue is First In First Out (FIFO) — elements are removed in the order they were added.
